title: First-Mile KPI Journal: Launch Milestones & Readiness Notes
body:
Purpose:
This 'First-Mile KPI Journal' collects the lightweight tracker, risk notes, and the small-run readiness checklist for the initial 2-week post-launch window (first-mile). The goal is to prioritize signals that matter for adoption and reliability without recreating the full launch playbook. Use this doc as the single place for daily stand notes and quick decision bullets during the initial activation window.

Summary snapshot (top-line, update cadence: daily AM):
- Primary goal: Validate product heuristics under 5k daily active sessions and keep token-level cost < $0.005 per response on average.
- Key success: Stable median latency <= 250ms P95 <= 800ms; error rate < 0.5%; new-user retention day-1 >= 22%.
- Canary cohort: 3% of traffic (internal + invited beta groups) then 15% gradual ramp if signals OK.
- Rollout timeline (high-level): internal smoke -> invite-only (3 days) -> expanded canary (2 days) -> 100% soft ramp (7 days) -> monitor & optimize.

Milestone ledger (owners noted; update on change):
1) Internal smoke (owner: Ravi Patel) — Completed. Quick smoke of infra, feature gating, and auth. Notes: prefix cache not enabled for dev env; ok for smoke.
2) Invite-only (owner: Talia Nguyen) — In progress. Target: 3% traffic, 200 sessions/day. Blockers: billing quotas review pending (Finance).
3) Canary expand to 15% (owner: Evan Brooks) — Ready to start after invite cohort 72h stable.
4) Soft ramp to 100% (owner: Maya Soto) — Contingency hold: if P95 latency > 900ms or error rate spike >1% for 30+ min, pause and fallback to previous served model variant.

Key metrics & current values (most recent measurement in parentheses):
- Daily active sessions (DAS): 1,150 (2024-11-19 AM)
- Median latency (ms): 210 (last 24h)
- P95 latency (ms): 670 (last 24h)
- API error rate: 0.28% (24h)
- Avg tokens / response: 142
- Token cost / response: $0.0046
- Day-1 retention (invited cohort): 26%
- Feature acceptance (first-time prompts completed): 63%
- Negative generation rate (toxic / fail): 1.1% — flagged for eval (quality team)

Mini-KPI tracker (daily lines — copy to spreadsheet when stable):
Date | DAS | Median(ms) | P95(ms) | Errors% | Tokens/resp | Cost/resp | Notes
2024-11-17 | 320 | 195 | 600 | 0.2 | 138 | $0.0045 | smoke ok
2024-11-18 | 780 | 205 | 640 | 0.25 | 140 | $0.0046 | invite start
2024-11-19 | 1,150 | 210 | 670 | 0.28 | 142 | $0.0046 | watching quality

Readiness checklist (quick toggle: green/amber/red, owner, comment):
- Routing policy verified (owner: Ravi Patel): green — smart routing in canary mode to fallback variant set.
- Quotas & billing verified (owner: Talia Nguyen): amber — finance approval for burst not yet cleared; manual throttle plan documented.
- Observability hooks (owner: Evan Brooks): green — token-level traces, latency breakdown and error sampling configured.
- Rollback plan ready (owner: Maya Soto): green — automatic fallback to 'small-model-v1' enabled and tested.
- Customer comms draft (owner: Product Marketing): amber — PMM review pending; hold on broad announcements.
- Security & audit logs (owner: Security): green — KMS logging for keys and access audit confirmed.

Rapid contingency playbook (if any single critical KPI crosses threshold):
Trigger thresholds (auto & manual):
- Latency P95 > 900ms for 30m -> initiate partial traffic shift to 10% + reduce batch sizes; if persists, rollback to previous model variant.
- Error rate > 1% sustained > 15m -> enable degraded-mode responses (shorter output), pause new sessions for non-essential routes.
- Token cost drift > 20% YoY baseline -> throttle non-critical batched jobs and enable cost-saver quantized variant for Dedicated pools.
- Day-1 retention drop > 10 percentage points -> freeze UI changes and open hot-fix ticket for product heuristics.

Signals to watch (daily):
- Token distribution (long tail of >400 tokens responses) — increases cost and latency
- Model fallback ratio (percentage of requests auto-failed to smaller model)
- Top 10 error messages (rate + stack traces)
- Cohort-specific retention (invited vs internal vs organic)
- Billing burn-rate estimate for next 72h (Finance)

Communication plan (who to ping & when):
- Immediate pager: SRE on-call + serving-runtime lead if error rate crosses 1%
- Slack channel: #launch-first-mile (updates every 2 hours until soft-ramp completed)
- Daily stand: 9:30 AM product-ops sync (owner summarizes)
- Exec pulse: single-line status at EOD to execs if any amber/red persists

Open questions / notes to self (raw):
- Short-term experiment: try KV prefetch for prompts with repeated context — might shave 30–40ms median. Add as optional A/B if stable by day 3.
- Consider toggling prefix-cache only for canary cohort to avoid cache priming effects across users.
- Revisit generation temperature by cohort — invited cohort tolerated higher creativity, but production should have lower variance.

Post-launch 14-day focus (what we will tighten):
- Day 1–3: stability & infra; triage bugs and regressions.
- Day 4–7: user flows + product telemetry conversion events; iterate prompt defaults if completion rates low.
- Day 8–14: cost optimizations (batching, quantization), model t-shirt sizing for Dedicated pools, and begin phased removal of guardrail throttles.

Decision log (short):
- 2024-11-10: Chose canary routing at 3% vs 1%: rationale = faster data for retention; risk = higher early cost. (owner: Maya Soto)
- 2024-11-16: Approve fallback to 'small-model-v1' for degraded traffic (owner: Ravi Patel)

Action items (next 48h):
- Talia: confirm finance burst window and update quotas (due 2024-11-21).
- Evan: add an alert that includes sample payloads when error rate > 0.5% (due 2024-11-20).
- Maya: finalize PMM announcement draft and hold for soft-ramp green (due 2024-11-22).

Appendix (quick links and checklist copies):
- Prelaunch runbook (confluence) -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/first-mile-launch-plan
- Canary cohort list (internal sheet) -> JIRA-PROD-8421 (permissions: product-ops + eng leads)
summary: Lightweight first-mile tracker for launch readiness, daily KPI snapshots, contingency triggers, and owner-run actions. Meant for product-ops to run daily checks during initial activation window.
